velden.kop: Zelensky warned airlines about drones over Russia, he did not threaten to shoot down aircraft
velden.oordeel_zin: Zelensky warned that Ukrainian drones are making Russian airspace unsafe, but explicitly added that Ukraine threatens not a single civilian aircraft [2] [3].
velden.bewering: Zelensky is now even threatening to shoot civilian aircraft out of the sky, which Ukraine of course already has experience with... #MH17
velden.kort: On 5 September a post circulated on X saying that Zelensky is threatening to shoot down civilian aircraft, with the hashtag MH17 attached [1]. On 1 September Zelensky warned airlines that Ukrainian drones are making Russian airspace unsafe, and said in the same speech that Ukraine threatens not a single civilian aircraft [2] [3]. As for MH17, the ICAO Council found Russia responsible in 2025 [10] [11].
velden.tekst:
The post appeared on Saturday 5 September at 12:51 on X [1]. It quotes an English post from a day earlier, with a 51-second video and the claim that Zelensky is threatening civilian aircraft [1]. The Dutch post turns that into him threatening to shoot them out of the sky, and refers with the hashtag MH17 to the 2014 disaster [1]. On 18 November the post had been viewed 14,721 times [1].

The post concerns Zelensky's evening address of Tuesday 1 September, with the video on Telegram and part of the text in English on X at 19:59 [13] [2]. In it he warned every airline that uses Russian airspace, every insurer and everyone who still uses the major Russian airports: the airspace will become completely unsafe [2] [3]. The reason he gave is Ukrainian drones, which will fly over Russia on such a scale that aviation will have to take them into account [3] [4]. Three days earlier he had ordered 1,000 drones a day against Russia [4].

In the same speech Zelensky said that Ukraine does not threaten civil aviation, "not a single civilian aircraft" [2]. In his own text, in English and Ukrainian, that sentence follows directly after the warning [2] [13]. Euronews and Meduza also report those words [3] [4]. According to him, Ukraine does not want innocent lives to be lost [2].

A day later Ukraine formally notified the ICAO, the United Nations aviation organization, that Russian airspace is unsafe [6]. The Turkish carriers Pegasus and Turkish Airlines cancelled flights to and from Moscow [6]. The same day the ICAO warned in general terms of a growing risk that civilian aircraft will be hit by weapons or caught in crossfire; it names neither Russia nor Ukraine [7].

Putin also saw a threat in it: he called the warning of 1 September state terrorism [5]. The reported plans of Ukraine concern closing the airspace, not shooting down aircraft. According to The Atlantic, quoted by The Insider, Ukraine was preparing a plan to shut down the airspace over Moscow with up to 1,000 drones in a single night, and Zelensky feared that a hit passenger plane would be seen as piracy [8]. According to Meduza, Zelensky's office called that report complete nonsense [14]. According to The Wall Street Journal, quoted by The Week, Ukraine wants to have drones circle near Russian airports so that takeoffs and landings come to a standstill [9]. That makes flying over Russia more dangerous. It is not a threat to shoot down aircraft.

MH17 was shot down on 17 July 2014 over eastern Ukraine with a Russian surface-to-air missile, over territory held by pro-Russian separatists [11]. 298 people were killed, including 196 Dutch nationals [11]. On 12 May 2025, in a case brought by the Netherlands and Australia, the ICAO Council ruled that Russia is responsible [10]. However, Russian and Ukrainian officials did name a missile as the cause of the disaster involving a Russian passenger plane over the Black Sea in October 2001, with 78 dead [12]. The Ukrainian official said it was probably by accident a missile from a Ukrainian exercise [12].
velden.niet_weten: The first sentence of the post, about which targets Russia and Ukraine hit, is a claim of its own that we do not check here. We found no fact-check of this claim by another newsroom, in seven languages and on more than twenty sites.
